data.rationale: parse_mode is called from git_tree__parse_raw (libgit2/src/tree.c:397) without any buffer_end parameter. Its loop `while ((c = *buffer++) != ' ')` at line 367 scans forward until it finds a space, with no bounds check against the end of the raw object data. If the input tree data contains no ' ' byte before its end, the loop keeps reading past the end of the heap allocation holding the fuzz input. Reachability: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput in fuzzers/objects_fuzzer.c calls git_object__from_raw with GIT_OBJ_TREE, which dispatches to git_tree__parse_raw on the raw fuzzer data. The standalone driver/libFuzzer place the input in an exact-size heap buffer, so the over-read is detected by ASan as heap-buffer-overflow. The caller's checks (`!buffer`, memchr bounds, OID size check) all happen after parse_mode returns, so they cannot prevent the initial over-read; a non-octal/non-space byte only returns -1 after the OOB byte was already read. The fix would be to pass buffer_end into parse_mode and bound the scan loop.
